name: ACT

certification.stepsNote: 4 jobs in the lineage; the 4th is the roar put publish step, excluded by --no-puts by design
certification.manifestDiff: 98/98 recorded pins present at the exact recorded version — 0 missing, 0 mismatched (23/97/73 per step); 135 distributions installed, 37 extra transitive
certification.manifestMethod: uv pip freeze --python <venv>/bin/python AND an importlib.metadata distribution count; both returned 135 and agree. pip freeze was NOT used — the reproduce venv is uv-provisioned and ships no pip, so it would return empty and read as 'nothing installed'.
certification.venvClosure: include-system-site-packages=false; sys.path carries no dist-packages and no host site-packages; torch, huggingface_hub, safetensors, numpy, trackio and wandb all resolve inside .venv. P0-14 absent, with the strongest available evidence: bare `python` does not exist on the host (host python3 is 3.10.12), yet the recorded `python ...` steps ran — so the recorded 3.12.10 venv demonstrably supplied the interpreter, and nothing was symlinked to fake it.
certification.bitIdenticalNote: model.safetensors is byte-for-byte the same SIZE as the capture (206,666,968 B) but a different sha256 — non-deterministic GPU training. We claim reproduce, not replicate.
certification.openObservation: torchcodec is a recorded pin but needs FFmpeg, an OS package no pip freeze captures; it fails to load on a bare host (libavutil.so.56-59 all absent) and LeRobot falls back to pyav, also a recorded pin. Did not affect this row's result.
certification.resultCaveat: Clean pass on the first attempt, no retries: exit 0 read from a file (not inferred from the log), 3/3 steps, 98/98 pins exact, outputs regenerated. Two things a reader should weigh. (1) The experiment link is NOT re-exercised by a rebuild in the way the capture exercised it: a rebuild host has no upload token, so the tracker falls back to local logging and uploads nothing. That is by design and is why the run still completes; it means the rebuild proves the logging code path runs, not that a second dashboard was produced. (2) torchcodec -> FFmpeg is an OS-package edge invisible to a pip freeze (P1-11); it is inert here only because LeRobot has a pyav fallback.

summary: ACT (Action Chunking Transformer, ResNet-18 backbone) trains end to end on the public lerobot/pusht_image dataset with zero lines of upstream source changed. Truncated to 300 of the 100000 default steps — a pipeline-viability run, not a converged policy. Two things bite anyone reproducing a framework rather than a script. First, the documented entry point only exists after `pip install -e .`, and an editable self-install makes the tracer treat the whole repository as package territory, so the lineage loses every data and checkpoint edge; the fix is to install the dependency extra, uninstall the package, and import from the checkout. Second — and this is the one that would have shipped an un-rebuildable row — `pip uninstall` leaves `src/lerobot.egg-info/` behind, and because the reproduction puts `src/` on sys.path, `importlib.metadata` reads it straight back as an installed `lerobot 0.6.2`, a version that has never been published on PyPI. Every structural check still passes; only trying to install the recorded environment finds it. Separately, upstream's own wandb logging is coupled to wandb's exact API in three places — `WandBLogger.__init__` forwards wandb's `resume=None` default and calls the wandb-only `wandb.run.get_url()` (wandb_utils.py:110,122), and `log_dict` calls `wandb.log(data=..., step=...)` using wandb's own keyword name (wandb_utils.py:202). Every one of those aborts a wandb-compatible substitute, which is why this row carried no experiment link for its first three captures. All three are now bridged, so the logging upstream already shipped is simply switched on, by three of its own flags and no source change — and the dashboard is live. Getting there surfaced the sharper lesson: the bridge picks its behaviour from an environment variable, and a tracked run records argv only, so setting that variable on the line above the command produces a run that succeeds at capture and fails on every rebuild with `AttributeError: '_Run' object has no attribute 'get_url'` — the credential-free fallback path implements a narrower object than the real one. Moving the assignment inside the recorded command is what makes the requirement travel with the lineage. A held-out eval step still runs alongside (eval_loss 0.529 over 2742 frames, matching training's own step-300 number), so the metric does not depend on the dashboard being reachable. This row was re-captured on 2026-08-11 on a newer capture toolchain that records a materially more complete package set: the download step's recorded environment went from 2 pins to 23, and a fresh clone installing exactly those 23 pins with --no-deps and PYTHONPATH unset now runs that step to exit 0. The earlier record's 2 pins could not — the step's own top-level import was missing from it.
experimentUrlNote: Upstream's own logging, enabled by three of upstream's own flags (--wandb.enable, --wandb.project, --wandb.disable_artifact) with zero lines of src/ changed. Verified by the RUN, not by a status code: the Space returns HTTP 200 for any query string, so a 200 proves nothing. Evidence that metrics actually landed: the traced child logged that the bridge took the real-tracker branch rather than its silent no-op stub; the upload token was asserted present in the task environment before any paid step; a token-less control run of the identical code path emits loud flush/upload failures and none of those strings appear in this run; and the backing store reports updatedAt 2026-08-11T01:51:04Z against a run that flushed at 01:51:01.

truncation.note: 300 of LeRobot's own default 100,000 training steps (TrainPipelineConfig.steps, src/lerobot/configs/train.py) — 0.3%. Same policy, dataset, batch size and seed as the default recipe; the step count was reduced, and --eval_steps was raised from its upstream default of 0 to 150 so that a run this short still computes a held-out metric. The published weights are a pipeline-viability run, not a converged policy.

truncationNote: 300 of LeRobot's own default 100,000 training steps (0.3%), batch 8, seed 1000. Reproduce, not replicate — a pipeline-viability run, not a converged policy; the published weights are not a quality result. Running the recorded recipe out to 100,000 steps is ~22h32m and ~$41.96 on the same instance; most of that is the held-out eval cadence this recipe adds, and restoring upstream's own --eval_steps default of 0 brings it to ~7h23m and ~$13.73.

fullRun.estimateBasis: Every term below was measured on this row — nothing is extrapolated from a headline figure. Hardware: 1x NVIDIA L40S (g6e.xlarge, us-east-2), $1.861/h on-demand. FIXED = 155.8s: cold start 44s (git clone + venv + install of all 98 recorded pins, measured by this row's own cold rebuild on a fresh host, not estimated) + fetch_dataset 4.5s + train-step overhead 24.3s (imports, dataset and policy construction, checkpoint save, tracker flush — this INCLUDES the ResNet-18 ImageNet backbone download, measured separately at 0.34s / 46,830,571 B, so it is counted rather than excluded) + evaluate 83.0s. That is 0.0433h = $0.08. VARIABLE has two terms, both measured, and identical on the capture host and the rebuild host: (1) the optimizer loop at step_s 0.264 s/step (LeRobot's own instrumentation: data_s 0.229 + updt_s 0.035), so 100,000 steps = 26,400s; (2) the held-out eval pass at 82s, which --eval_steps=150 triggers floor(100000/150) = 666 times = 54,612s. TOTAL 81,168s = 22h32m = $41.96, i.e. $0.0004188 per step ($0.0001365 optimizer + $0.0002822 amortised eval). IMPORTANT: the eval term is the larger of the two and it is a property of THIS recipe, not of LeRobot. Upstream's own default is eval_steps=0 (TrainPipelineConfig, src/lerobot/configs/train.py) — no held-out passes at all; --eval_steps=150 was added here so that a 300-step run would still compute a metric. Restoring that upstream default and running the same 100,000 steps costs 26,556s = 7h23m = $13.73. Both numbers are published because the reader's path is `roar reproduce --script` followed by an edit: changing only --steps=300 to 100000 gives $41.96; also restoring --eval_steps to its upstream default gives $13.73.

issues.title: `pip uninstall` leaves `src/<pkg>.egg-info` behind, and a `src/`-layout project makes it live again
`WandBLogger` is coupled to wandb's exact API, so a substitute must shim three call shapes
`torchcodec` is a hard dependency of `lerobot[dataset]` but cannot load without system FFmpeg
`--eval_steps` runs a *full* pass over the held-out split, which dominates wall clock on a truncated run
Checkpoint layout is derived, not configurable — the publish path has to be predicted before the run
